concepts.name: Alkanes & Alkenes: Additions & Named Reactions
concepts.summary: Wurtz reaction couples alkyl halides to form symmetrical alkanes. Markovnikov addition: electrophilic proton adds to carbon with more hydrogens. Anti-Markovnikov (peroxide effect) occurs ONLY with $\text{HBr}$ in the presence of peroxides via free radical mechanism. Ozonolysis cleaves $>\text{C=C}<$ into aldehydes and ketones.
concepts.common_traps: The peroxide effect applies strictly to $\text{HBr}$; it DOES NOT work with $\text{HCl}$ or $\text{HI}$ due to thermodynamic and kinetic bond enthalpy constraints.
concepts.tips_and_tricks: Ozonolysis products directly reveal the position of the double bond: replace $>\text{C=O}$ and $\text{O=C}<$ with a double bond to reconstruct the starting alkene.

concepts.name: Alkynes & Aromatic Electrophilic Substitution
concepts.summary: Acidity of terminal alkynes: $sp$-hybridized carbon has $50\%$ $s$-character, making terminal hydrogen acidic enough to react with $\text{NaNH}_2$ or ammoniacal $\text{AgNO}_3$. Hydration of acetylene with $\text{Hg}^{2+}/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives acetaldehyde; propyne gives acetone. Electrophilic aromatic substitution on benzene: Nitration (electrophile $\text{NO}_2^+$ generated by $\text{HNO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$), Friedel-Crafts alkylation/acylation with anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$.
concepts.common_traps: Aniline cannot undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction because its basic $-\text{NH}_2$ group coordinates with the Lewis acid catalyst $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form an inactive salt complex.
concepts.tips_and_tricks: Terminal alkynes give a red precipitate of copper acetylide with ammoniacal cuprous chloride, distinguishing them from non-terminal alkynes.

### 2.1 Alkanes & Alkenes: Additions & Named Reactions (Hydrocarbons)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **15 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Wurtz reaction couples alkyl halides to form symmetrical alkanes. Markovnikov addition: electrophilic proton adds to carbon with more hydrogens. Anti-Markovnikov (peroxide effect) occurs ONLY with $\text{HBr}$ in the presence of peroxides via free radical mechanism. Ozonolysis cleaves $>	ext{C=C}<$ into aldehydes and ketones.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{Wurtz: } 2\text{RX} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{R-R} + 2\text{NaX}, \quad \text{Ozonolysis: } >\text{C=C}< \xrightarrow{\text{O}_3, \text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}} >\text{C=O} + \text{O=C}<
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: The peroxide effect applies strictly to $\text{HBr}$; it DOES NOT work with $\text{HCl}$ or $\text{HI}$ due to thermodynamic and kinetic bond enthalpy constraints.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Ozonolysis products directly reveal the position of the double bond: replace $>	ext{C=O}$ and $\text{O=C}<$ with a double bond to reconstruct the starting alkene.

- **[2025 Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"The major product formed when $1-$ Bromo $-3-$ Chlorocyclobutane reacts with metallic sodium in dry ether is..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2024 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"2-methyl propane can be prepared by Wurtz reaction. The haloalkanes taken along with metallic sodium and dry ether are :..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2024 Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"In the given sequence of reactions, identify ' $P^{'},Q^{'},R^{'}$ and ' $S$ respectively...."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

### 2.2 Alkynes & Aromatic Electrophilic Substitution (Alkynes & Aromatics)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **0 PYQs** (Standard Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Acidity of terminal alkynes: $sp$-hybridized carbon has $50\%$ $s$-character, making terminal hydrogen acidic enough to react with $\text{NaNH}_2$ or ammoniacal $\text{AgNO}_3$. Hydration of acetylene with $\text{Hg}^{2+}/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives acetaldehyde; propyne gives acetone. Electrophilic aromatic substitution on benzene: Nitration (electrophile $\text{NO}_2^+$ generated by $\text{HNO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$), Friedel-Crafts alkylation/acylation with anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{Acidity: } \text{CH}\equiv\text{CH} > \text{CH}_2\text{=CH}_2 > \text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_3, \quad \text{Nitration Electrophile: } \text{NO}_2^+
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Aniline cannot undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction because its basic $-\text{NH}_2$ group coordinates with the Lewis acid catalyst $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form an inactive salt complex.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Terminal alkynes give a red precipitate of copper acetylide with ammoniacal cuprous chloride, distinguishing them from non-terminal alkynes.

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring KCET Pitfalls in Hydrocarbons

### 1. Speed & 80-Second Constraint Management
KCET demands answering 60 questions in 80 minutes (~1.33 minutes per question). The most lethal trap is spending 3+ minutes on long algebraic derivations. Always check for dimensional consistency or option substitution first.

### 2. NCERT & Karnataka PU Board Direct Lines
Over 45% of KCET theory questions are taken directly from NCERT / Karnataka PU Board textbook summary points, margins, and standard exemplar questions. Pay rigorous attention to exceptions (e.g., electron gain enthalpy of Cl vs F, acidic nature of boric acid, non-polar symmetrical geometries).

### 3. Unit Conversions & Prefix Overlooks
Units of molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), micro/nano multipliers (10^-6, 10^-9), and centimeter-to-meter conversions in optics and gravitation account for the highest frequency of careless mark losses in KCET.

### 4. No Negative Marking Advantage
Since KCET has NO negative marking, never leave any question unattempted. When down to two options, use dimensional elimination or parity checks to maximize expected score.
